plan.title: bug(installer,doctor): whole-scope @deftai→GitHub Packages breaks public @deftai/directive-runtime install/repair (split-registry honesty)

narratives.Description: OVPR fix plan unit P2-U10 (story id ovpr-p2-u10), spec units/P2-U10-split-registry-install-repair.md, issue #6141, decision D-009 (message only). When `@deftai:registry` points at a private registry, Directive's two public packages 404 and `directive upgrade --dry-run` fails before any plan with npm's raw E404 (reproduced on 0.129.14), while doctor advises remapping the whole scope, which breaks the project's other @deftai packages. Doctor gets a split-scope finding, the launcher adds a hint (cause, do not remap the scope, the one-run `npm_config_@deftai:registry` override) on a real registry miss, and UPGRADING.md lists only the two published packages.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Repos whose `.npmrc` maps the entire `@deftai` scope to GitHub Packages (for an internal package such as `@deftai/rivet-os`) cannot install or repair `@deftai/directive` / `@deftai/directive-runtime` from the public npm registry. Doctor `npm-registry-mirror` steers “point `@deftai` at registry.npmjs.org,” which would break the internal package.

## Source

Broken out from closed multi-finding bag **#5845** (2026-11-09). One issue → one ticket.

## Expected

OVPR install/repair/doctor messaging works with a **split** registry: public packages (`@deftai/directive`, `@deftai/directive-runtime`) from registry.npmjs.org; other `@deftai/*` may stay on GitHub Packages. Prefer lockfile / package-specific registry guidance over “remap the whole scope.”

## Actual

`directive install --repair` / launcher fetches hit `npm.pkg.github.com` for `directive-runtime` → 404. Doctor recovery fights the consumer’s legitimate split.

## Ownership

OVPR / installer — assignee polfer.

## Refs

#5845 (closed glom); related doctor registry prose.

narratives.UserStory: As a developer whose .npmrc routes the whole @deftai scope to a private registry, I want doctor and the launcher to explain the split-scope failure and give an override that does not break my other @deftai packages, so that I can install or upgrade Directive without remapping my scope.

narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/doctor/npm-registry.ts runNpmRegistryMirrorCheck: when the scoped key routes @deftai to a non-public registry and package.json has other @deftai/* dependencies, return a new `split-scope` status with the unit spec's message; never print the configured URL. Other cases keep today's advice but name only @deftai/directive and @deftai/directive-runtime.
2. New packages/cli/src/registry-hint.ts scopedRegistryHint(projectRoot, blob): only when the effective @deftai:registry is non-public and the blob is a registry miss for a Directive package (E404, 404 Not Found, ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404, ETARGET, ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION), return one hint: cause, do not remap the scope in .npmrc, the one-run override `npm_config_@deftai:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` (POSIX form plus one PowerShell line). Read config with the same no-shell read as doctor.
3. Call it from bookends.ts reportPmFailure() and from the resolveLatestStableVersion() / resolvePublishedContract() failure paths in runFirstInstall() / runUpgrade(), so `directive upgrade --dry-run` shows the hint. For repair with lockOk the hint names `npm ci` / `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first.
4. content/UPGRADING.md 'Corporate or mirrored npm registry': list only the two published packages, add a split-scope paragraph, and say 'leave the project directory' applies to the global launcher only.
5. Tests per the spec. Changelog fragment changelog.d/6141-split-registry-hint.md.
Scope: Five production files at most; registry.ts only if the hint is attached there rather than in bookends.ts.
narratives.Constraint:
- Never write `.npmrc`, user npm config, or pnpm config (AC5.8).
- Never print the configured registry URL or tokens (the public npmjs URL in the override is fine).
- Do not use `npm ci` for install or upgrade (AC5.11).
- Do not change `runRepair()` to restore from the lockfile (Q1 = A, D-009).
- Do not change `RECOVERY_GUIDANCE` or the launcher doctor's missing-runtime text; that is the Rule 3 message table (P4-U3b / P4-U3c).
- Do not add a "Directive registry" setting or any per-package registry mechanism.
- Do not force npmjs for Directive's own packages in the launcher (rejected in D-009; breaks AC5.8).
- OVPR change gate: read ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/OVPR-CHANGE-GATE.md. Do not edit docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/ and do not ship behaviour that departs from the written OVPR requirements or architecture; stop that part and hand back a change proposal.
- Changelog: add the changelog.d fragment named in file_scope; never edit CHANGELOG.md.

issueCommentThread.body:
Consumer evidence from `deftai/deftvisage` (2026-11-16). It is stuck on 0.126.2 because of this bug.

## Setup

`.npmrc` sends the whole scope to GitHub Packages for `@deftai/rivet-os`. It also tries to send the directive packages to public npm, one line per package:

```
@deftai:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
@deftai/directive:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
@deftai/directive-core:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
@deftai/directive-types:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
@deftai/directive-content:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
```

npm ignores registry keys for single packages. Only scope keys work. So every `@deftai/*` package still goes to GitHub Packages. Even `--registry=https://registry.npmjs.org` on the command line loses to the scope key:

```
$ npm view @deftai/directive-runtime version
npm error 404 Not Found - GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@deftai%2fdirective-runtime - npm package "directive-runtime" does not exist under owner "deftai"

$ npm view @deftai/directive version --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
npm error 404 Not Found - GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@deftai%2fdirective
```

## Current workaround (works only up to 0.126.x)

- `tools/deft-cli/` is a separate package with its own lockfile. It pins `@deftai/directive@^0.126.1`, and its lockfile `resolved` URLs point at `registry.npmjs.org`.
- CI installs the CLI with `npm i -g "@deftai/directive@${V}" "@deftai/directive-core@${V}" --@deftai:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`.

This works only while `@deftai/directive` carries `directive-core` and `directive-content` as dependencies. 0.126.2 is the last version that does. From 0.127.0 to 0.129.10 the package is a launcher with `dependencies: {}` that hands off to a project-local `@deftai/directive-runtime`. Installing that runtime uses the project's registry settings and returns the 404 above. So no newer version can be adopted.

## What `deft update` does here

With the global 0.126.2, `deft update --dry-run` reports `update_state: "current"`. It does not offer the move to the runtime layout, and it does not mention the registry split. The project deposit is at `.deft/core/VERSION` `v0.104.0` (`managed_by: npm`).

## What would unblock us

Any one of these:
1. The launcher installs `@deftai/directive-runtime` with an explicit `--@deftai:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org` for that one install, so the lockfile records the npmjs `resolved` URL and later `npm ci` works.
2. Directive packages are also published to GitHub Packages under `deftai`, so the whole-scope mapping finds them.
3. Doctor and repair text describe the split and offer one of the two above. Today they say to move the whole scope to npmjs, which breaks `rivet-os`.

Also, `classifyPinVersion` in the launcher classifies a tarball URL pin as `invalid`, so pinning the runtime to an npmjs tarball URL in `package.json` is not a workaround either.
